overall_summary: Analysis of 46 videos reveals that high-stakes planetary physics, time-bounded '5-second' scenarios, and planetary orbital/scale comparisons (Saturn, Sun, Atmosphere) drive the highest view counts and average view percentages (AVP). Videos with AVP above 60-70% systematically leverage visual impact hooks and seamless looping, as seen in top performers like 'What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn?' (1,038 views) and 'What If Earth Lost Its Atmosphere for 5 Seconds?' (881 views, 64.26% AVP). Conversely, micro-scale or abstract topics ('Wi-Fi signals', 'Cosmic Dust', 'Water to Mercury') underperform significantly in retention and impressions.

what_is_working.evidence: 'What If Earth Lost Its Atmosphere for 5 Seconds?' achieved 881 views and 64.26% AVP; 'What If the Sun Blinked Off for 5 Seconds?' achieved 71.59% AVP and 66 estimated minutes watched.
what_is_working.action: Standardize high-stakes '5 Seconds' or '10 Seconds' time constraints across curiosity triggers to create immediate urgency and digestible narrative structures.

what_is_working.evidence: 'What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn?' generated 1,038 views (50.75% AVP), and 'What If Earth Swapped Orbits With Ice Giants' achieved 73.89% AVP (43s AVD).
what_is_working.action: Focus title formulas on familiar solar system bodies (Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Sun) interacting through drastic orbital or physical transformations.

what_is_working.pattern: High initial watch ratios (seamless loop hooks)
what_is_working.evidence: 'What If Solar Wind Hit Earth at Light Speed?' maintained an audience watch ratio >2.0 in the first 7% of video progress, yielding 94.95% AVP.
what_is_working.action: Craft audio-visual hooks that seamlessly bridge the final second back into the first frame to force instant looping.

what_to_improve.evidence: 'What If You Could See Every Wi-Fi Signal?' (41 views) and 'What If Earth Passed Through Cosmic Dust?' (53 views, 39.94% AVP) failed to generate initial click momentum.
what_to_improve.action: Avoid abstract electromagnetic or chemical scenarios; restrict topics to immediate, visually striking planetary-scale physics.

what_to_improve.pattern: Immediate progress 0.01-0.10 drop-offs on instant gravity/fluid shifts
what_to_improve.evidence: 'What If Earth's Gravity Reversed For 5 Seconds?' saw relative retention drop from 0.30 to 0.13 between progress 0.01 and 0.10.
what_to_improve.action: Eliminate introductory setup frames; show the visual transformation occurring in the very first 0.5 seconds of video.

retention_insights.drop_or_strength: Extreme initial audience watch ratio (>1.45 to 4.50)
retention_insights.evidence: 'What If the Sun Blinked Off for 5 Seconds?' started at 1.45 audience watch ratio and held 0.65 at 49% progress. 'What If Earth's Core Froze Solid for 5 Seconds?' recorded 361.81% AVP due to rewatches.
retention_insights.action: Design visual payoff frames at the midpoint (20-30s) and resolve immediately prior to the ending frame to maximize multi-pass view behavior.

retention_insights.evidence: 'What If Earth's Atmosphere Turned to Liquid?' plummeted from 1.14 audience watch ratio to 0.50 by progress 0.26 and ended at 39.43% AVP.
retention_insights.action: Replace static explanatory visual graphics in the first 3 seconds with active, motion-dense visual simulations.

best_posting_windows.reason: Yielded top performing videos including 'What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn?' (1,038 views), 'What If Sound Could Travel Through Space?' (701 views), and 'What If Venus Swapped Orbits' (427 views).
Consistently produced high views and engagement, including 'What If Earth Lost Its Atmosphere for 5 Seconds?' (881 views) and 'What If an Asteroid Smashed Through the Moon?' (395 views).
